nuggets.title: Runtime Script Tag Order Breaks Shared Shell

scenario.symptoms: Checkout micro-frontend loads before shell router; white screen on 20% of page loads due to race.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Teams inject bundles via unordered async script tags without module federation manifest orchestration.

incident.headline: Unorchestrated script loading races break shell composition

agenda.goal: Detail the specific mechanism used to compose the application at runtime.
agenda.opener: How exactly are the different teams' JavaScript bundles composed into a single running application?

evidence.strong: Evaluates runtime composition via Module Federation or import maps, explaining the mechanics of remote entry resolution.
evidence.adequate: Chooses a runtime method but lacks depth on how the browser actually resolves the dependencies.
evidence.weak: Proposes build-time NPM packages, completely violating the independent deployment requirement.

misconceptions.pattern: Believing NPM packages allow independent deployments.
misconceptions.challenge: If Team A updates their NPM package, how does that change reach the live production site?

probes: How does the host app execute the remote code?
What format are these bundles served in?
hints: Think about modern bundler features that allow dynamic code loading.
How does Webpack 5 handle sharing code between separate builds?
agenda.referenceFix: Chose a runtime composition mechanism like Module Federation to enable independent deploys.

nuggets.title: Users Download React Four Times on One Page

scenario.symptoms: Lighthouse shows 1.2MB duplicate React bundles from four micro-frontends on dashboard.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Each MFE bundles its own React version; shared dependency config not enforced in build pipeline.

incident.headline: Duplicate shared library bundles inflate page weight

agenda.goal: Design a strategy to share heavy libraries without causing version conflicts or redundant downloads.
agenda.opener: If multiple teams use React and the same design system, how do you prevent the user from downloading these libraries multiple times?

evidence.strong: Proposes singletons for core libraries, defines a strict sharing contract, and handles fallback if versions mismatch.
evidence.adequate: Mentions sharing libraries via a CDN or bundler but misses the singleton requirement for stateful frameworks.
evidence.weak: Forces every micro-frontend to bundle its own dependencies, leading to massive performance hits.

misconceptions.pattern: Attempting to share every single library across all teams.
misconceptions.challenge: What happens to team autonomy if they have to coordinate updating a minor utility library?

probes: React crashes if two copies are running. How do you guarantee only one copy is instantiated?
How is the design system package distributed and versioned?
hints: Module Federation has a 'shared' configuration. How does it work?
Consider the difference between libraries that maintain internal state and pure utility libraries.
agenda.referenceFix: Set up shared dependency singletons for core frameworks while letting teams bundle specific utilities.

nuggets.title: Team A Exception Crashes Entire Shell

scenario.symptoms: Uncaught TypeError in recommendations widget takes down navigation and payments MFEs.
scenario.interviewerSetup: All micro-frontends share same JS realm without error boundaries or iframe sandbox isolation.

incident.headline: Missing fault isolation lets one MFE crash entire application shell

agenda.goal: Ensure failures in one micro-frontend do not cascade to the shell or other micro-frontends.
agenda.opener: Let's say Team A ships a bug that causes an unhandled JavaScript exception. What happens to the rest of the page?

evidence.strong: Uses framework Error Boundaries to catch render errors, provides graceful fallbacks, and uses CSS modules or Shadow DOM for style isolation.
evidence.adequate: Mentions catching errors but misses style leakage or infinite loop protections.
evidence.weak: Allows a single broken component to white-screen the entire application.

misconceptions.pattern: Believing window.onerror is sufficient to recover the UI.
misconceptions.challenge: If a React component throws during render, how does a global error handler restore the rest of the component tree?

probes: How do you prevent Team B's CSS from overwriting Team A's buttons?
What if a micro-frontend takes 10 seconds to respond?
hints: How does React natively handle component crashes?
How can you scope CSS so it doesn't leak globally?
agenda.referenceFix: Applied error boundaries and scoped CSS to strictly isolate micro-frontend failures.

nuggets.title: Global Window Events Break Cross-Team Contracts

scenario.symptoms: Cart MFE listens to ad-hoc window events; refactor in checkout team breaks cart count silently.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Cross-MFE communication uses undocumented global CustomEvents instead of versioned event bus.

incident.headline: Ad-hoc global events create fragile cross-MFE coupling

agenda.goal: Establish a decoupled contract for cross-micro-frontend communication.
agenda.opener: How do two micro-frontends on the same page share state or communicate with each other?

evidence.strong: Proposes a decoupled event bus or explicit prop passing via the shell, avoiding shared global state.
evidence.adequate: Suggests storing state in local storage or the URL without a clear notification mechanism.
evidence.weak: Tries to share a single global state store across independent builds, tightly coupling all teams.

misconceptions.pattern: Using a single global Redux store for all teams.
misconceptions.challenge: If Team A changes their state shape, how do you prevent Team B's code from breaking?

probes: How do you ensure the event payloads don't introduce tight coupling?
What if the receiving micro-frontend hasn't loaded yet when the event fires?
hints: How do native DOM elements communicate?
Consider a publish-subscribe pattern isolated to the browser.
agenda.referenceFix: Designed a decoupled event bus for cross-app communication.

nuggets.title: Stale Manifest Serves Old MFE After Deploy

scenario.symptoms: Team ships fix but users still hit broken bundle for 30 minutes; CDN and manifest cache not invalidated together.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Shell fetches manifest cached 24h at edge while MFE bundle URL version not tied to manifest epoch.

incident.headline: Manifest and asset cache skew delays MFE deploy visibility

agenda.goal: Design the deployment lifecycle, from code push to updating the registry/manifest.
agenda.opener: Walk me through the exact steps when a team clicks deploy. How does their new code reach the live shell?

evidence.strong: Describes building assets, uploading to a CDN with content hashes, and updating a central manifest that the shell fetches dynamically.
evidence.adequate: Mentions deploying to a CDN but is vague on how the shell discovers there is a new version.
evidence.weak: Requires rebuilding the entire shell app to deploy a child micro-frontend.

probes: How do you roll back a bad deployment instantly?
How does the shell fetch the latest manifest without caching stale versions?
hints: The shell needs to know the exact URL of the new JavaScript file.
Where is the mapping between the section name and its bundle URL stored?
agenda.referenceFix: Outlined a manifest-driven deployment flow with content-hashed CDN assets.
